newsitem.title: FRANCE: Renault says complied with Belgian law.
newsitem.headline: Renault says complied with Belgian law.

text.p: Renault chairman Louis Schweitzer told a French parliamentary committee on Tuesday that the French carmaker had complied with Belgian law in announcing the closure late last month of the Vilvoorde plant.
In a statement issued after Schweitzer's appearance, the committee said he had pointed out distinctions in Belgian law, which requires negotiations for staff cuts but not for plant closures.

Renault said it told the works council of the Vilvoorde plant about the closure shortly before announcing it to the media. In addition to closing the Vilvoorde plant, which employs 3,100, Renault also plans to cut 2,764 jobs this year in France.

In regard to the French job cuts, Schweitzer told the committee that the Robien law, which provides assistance for companies which shorten working hours to preserve jobs, was geared to temporary slowdowns in production.

"It does not address the objective of permanently reducing the cost of labour, and a reduction in jobs proportional to work schedules does not seem negotiable," the statement quoted Schweitzer as saying. He said early retirements seemed the best approach given the "unacceptable" nature of layoffs.

Schweitzer and his counterpart at PSA Peugeot Citroen, Jacques Calvet, appealed to the government last year for assistance in carrying out a massive early retirement plan entailing 40,000 jobs, but the government turned them down.
